title: Book 5 — Terpsichore, Chapter 115
paragraphs: The Amathusians accordingly have continued to do so even to my day. But the Ionians who had fought the sea-battle in Cyprus, when they perceived that the fortunes of Onesilus were ruined and that the cities of the Cyprians—except Salamis—were under siege, and that Salamis had been handed back by the Salaminians to Gorgus the former king, sailed away back to Ionia as soon as they realized this. Of the cities in Cyprus, Soli held out longest under siege, and the Persians took it in the fifth month by undermining the wall around it.
